arxiv-2110-03911.title: Nonlinear sequential fractional boundary value problems involving generalized ψ \psi -Caputo fractional derivatives
arxiv-2110-03911.creator: Nguyen Minh Dien
arxiv-2110-03911.description: Abstract This paper is devoted to study the nonlinear sequential fractional boundary value problems involving generalized ψ \psi -Caputo fractional derivatives with nonlocal boundary conditions. We investigate the Green function and some of its properties, from which we obtain a new Lyapunov-type inequality for our problem. A lower bound for the possible eigenvalues of our problem is derived.

arxiv-2301-02116.title: Simulated performance of the molecular mapping for young giant exoplanets with the Medium Resolution Spectrometer of JWST/MIRI
arxiv-2301-02116.creator: M. Mâlin, A. Boccaletti, B. Charnay, F. Kiefer, B. Bézard
arxiv-2301-02116.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by M. Mâlin, A. Boccaletti, B. Charnay, F. Kiefer, B. Bézard. Young giant planets are the best targets for characterization with direct imaging. The Medium Resolution Spectrometer (MRS) of the Mid-Infrared Instrument (MIRI) of the recently launched James Webb Space Telescope ( JWST ) will give access to the first spectroscopic data for direct imaging above 5 μ \muup m with unprecedented sensitivity at a spectral resolution up to 3700.

arxiv-2402-09269.title: Personalized Large Language Models
arxiv-2402-09269.creator: Stanisław Woźniak, Bartłomiej Koptyra, Arkadiusz Janz, Przemysław Kazienko and Jan Kocoń
arxiv-2402-09269.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have significantly advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks in recent years. However, their universal nature poses limitations in scenarios requiring personalized responses, such as recommendation systems and chatbots. This paper investigates methods to personalize LLMs, comparing fine-tuning and zero-shot reasoning approaches on subjective tasks.

arxiv-2501-11473.title: Bounds on the Privacy Amplification of Arbitrary Channels via the Contraction of f α f_{\alpha} -Divergence Thanks: This work was supported by the Swedish Research Council (VR) under grants 2023-04787 and 2024-06615.
arxiv-2501-11473.creator: Leonhard Grosse 1 , Sara Saeidian 1 2 , Tobias J. Oechtering 1 , and Mikael Skoglund 1
arxiv-2501-11473.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Leonhard Grosse 1 , Sara Saeidian 1 2 , Tobias J. Oechtering 1 , and Mikael Skoglund 1. We examine the privacy amplification of channels that do not necessarily satisfy any LDP guarantee by analyzing their contraction behavior in terms of f α f_{\alpha} -divergence, an f f -divergence related to Rényi-divergence via a monotonic transformation.

arxiv-2512-12850.title: KANELÉ: Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks for Efficient LUT-based Evaluation Conference: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM/SIGDA International Symposium on Field Programmable Gate Arrays; February 22–24, 2026; Seaside, CA, USA Proceedings of the 2026 ACM/SIGDA International Symposium on Field Programmable Gate A
arxiv-2512-12850.creator: Duc Hoang, Aarush Gupta, Philip Harris
arxiv-2512-12850.description: Abstract . Low-latency, resource-efficient neural network inference on FPGAs is essential for applications demanding real-time capability and low power. Lookup table (LUT)-based neural networks are a common solution, combining strong representational power with efficient FPGA implementation. In this work, we introduce KANELÉ, a framework that exploits the unique properties of Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (KANs) for FPGA deployment.

arxiv-2602-15648.title: Guided Diffusion by Optimized Loss Functions on Relaxed Parameters for Inverse Material Design
arxiv-2602-15648.creator: Jens U. Kreber jens.kreber@uni-a.de, Christian Weißenfels christian.weissenfels@uni-a.de, Joerg Stueckler joerg.stueckler@uni-a.de
arxiv-2602-15648.description: Abstract Inverse design problems are common in engineering and materials science. The forward direction, i.e., computing output quantities from design parameters, typically requires running a numerical simulation, such as a FEM, as an intermediate step, which is an optimization problem by itself. In many scenarios, several design parameters can lead to the same or similar output values.

pmc-11437209.creator: L Bouby, V Bonhomme, S Ivorra, R Bacilieri, S Ben Makhad, E Bonnaire, M Cabanis, M Derreumaux, M F Dietsch-Sellami, F Durand, A Evin, I Figueiral, L Flottes, C Hallavant, F Jedrusiak, T Lacombe, P Marinval, L Martin, V Matterne, C Pagnoux, T Pastor, R Pinaud, B Pradat, S Preiss, J Ros, N Rovira, M P
pmc-11437209.description: The cultivation of grapevines has spanned millennia, leading to thousands of varieties through exchanges, mutations, and crosses between genotypes, as well probably as gene flow from wild populations. These varieties are typically categorized by regional origin and primary use, either for wine production or fruit consumption.

pmc-12661799.title: Mass spectrometry-based proteomics of FFPE tissues: progress, limitations, and clinical translation barriers
pmc-12661799.creator: Sara Abdulmohsen AlHammadi, Lamar Nabil Nagshabandi, Huzaifa Muhammad, Hatouf H Sukkarieh, Ahmad Aljada
pmc-12661799.description: BackgroundFormalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue proteomics has emerged as a promising approach for precision medicine, offering access to vast clinical archives. Despite technological advances enabling identification of thousands of proteins from FFPE samples, no proteomic diagnostic tests based on FFPE tissues have achieved regulatory approval for clinical diagnostics, raising fundamental questions about the translational viability of this approach.

pmc-13169971.title: The effects of artificial intelligence ethics awareness, digital literacy, and metacognition on nursing students’ attitudes toward artificial intelligence
pmc-13169971.creator: Chohee Bang, Yujin Hur
pmc-13169971.description: BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming healthcare, raising new ethical challenges related to patient rights, transparency, and fairness. Nursing students must therefore develop competencies not only in digital and cognitive skills but also in AI ethics awareness to ensure responsible adoption of these technologies.MethodsA descriptive correlational study was conducted with 121 nursing students in South Korea.

pmc-13219168.title: Sex differences modulate olfactory bulb volume–function relationships but not olfactory training-induced plasticity
pmc-13219168.creator: Yi-Ting Hsieh, Yin-Chun Liao, Heather Grace Piluden Dulnuan, Jiing-Feng Lirng, Yun-Ting Chao
pmc-13219168.description: Men typically display larger olfactory bulb (OB) volumes, while women demonstrate superior olfactory performance. Olfactory training (OT) has been shown to induce structural changes in OB, but whether sex influences OT-related plasticity remains unclear. This study aimed to examine how sex differences modulate OB volume–function relationships and OT-related OB neuroplasticity.

pmc-13333138.title: Multifocal Skeletal Muscle Mineralisation Following Severe Trauma and Prolonged Critical Illness: A Case Report
pmc-13333138.creator: Mohammed Uddin, Jawad Naqvi, Sohaib I Uddin, Ayesha Amal
pmc-13333138.description: Soft tissue mineralisation is an uncommon complication of severe trauma and critical illness and may occur in association with metabolic derangements, tissue injury and prolonged immobilisation. We present a case of a 26-year-old male patient who developed extensive skeletal muscle calcification following multiple stab wounds, hypovolemic shock, and surgical interventions, including limb amputation and bowel resections.

pmc-13710601.title: Side-to-side differences in hip bone mineral density and associated morphological factors
pmc-13710601.creator: Keisuke Uemura, Yoshito Otake, Mazen Soufi, Sotaro Kono, Ryo Higuchi, Tomoki Asano, Hirokazu Mae, Tetsuro Tani, Kazuma Takashima, Yoshinobu Sato, Seiji Okada, Hidetoshi Hamada
pmc-13710601.description: SummaryIn the analysis of 82 participants using quantitative computed tomography (QCT) images, side-to-side differences in hip bone mineral density were 3.0%. Gluteal muscle volume and femoral anteversion asymmetry contributed to these discrepancies. Bilateral hip assessment may improve the detection of osteoporosis, particularly when QCT data are available.PurposeSide-to-side differences in hip bone mineral density (BMD) are occasionally observed in clinical practice.
